title: deferred-trace-ingest-sidecar-queueing-and-rehydration
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem: During periodic downstream outages (Tempo/Jaeger), high-cardinality tenants saw large span loss or expensive replays. We need a first-class sidecar/worker pattern that accepts OTLP traces, durably queues tenant-scoped envelopes (small local cache + S3 fallback), and rehydrates/forwards when the downstream is healthy. The intent is to reduce data loss, avoid large burst replays that blow throughput, and provide tenant-level throttling and prioritization.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar accepts OTLP/gRPC and HTTP spans and writes tenant-scoped envelopes to local write-ahead queue (WAL)
WAL size configurable per-tenant and will spill to S3-compatible backend with encryption
Forwarder replays queued envelopes respecting tenant priority, global rate limit, and downstream health signals
Replay implements exponential backoff + jitter and checkpointing so replays are resumable after restart
Grafana dashboard shows queued-envelopes, replay-rate, drop-rate, and per-tenant backlog with alert rule for >12h retention
Integration tests simulate Tempo outage and verify no loss for medium-priority tenants and controlled shedding for low-priority
E2E load test demonstrates that replay windows do not exceed console SLA (99th perc latency target) under 3x normal backlog
notes: Design: lightweight sidecar written in Go, reuses existing WAL proto used by ENG-271001 to stay compatible with durable-buffering work
Queue format: gzipped, tenant-prefixed envelope with metadata (tenant_id, priority, original_timestamp, schema_version)
Backpressure path: when local WAL exceeds threshold, sidecar triggers HTTP 429 to upstream OTLP agents with Retry-After and records shed metrics
Spill-to-S3: use v2 auth role with KMS; objects stored with tenant prefix + hourly buckets to simplify retention/GC
Security: all persisted envelopes encrypted at rest using customer/KMS keys when running in Private deployments (configurable)
Trade-offs: local WAL reduces cloud egress but increases host disk usage; we cap per-host WAL to avoid noisy-neighbor disk exhaustion
Observability hooks: expose Prometheus metrics and a /debug/queue endpoint for sampling first N envelopes (redacted) for debugging
Compatibility: will accept both OTLP collector format and legacy Jaeger thrift-over-HTTP encoded spans and convert to canonical envelope
implementation_plan: Week 1: Proto + WAL library extraction and unit tests
Week 2: Sidecar gRPC/HTTP server + local queueing + basic replay loop
Week 3: S3 spill integration, checkpointing persistence, and resilience (crash/restart tests)
Week 4: Integrate downstream health-check signals from Tempo metrics endpoint and add rate limiter
Week 5: Staging rollout behind feature flag, create dashboard and alerts, run chaos test simulating Tempo flaps
risks: Disk exhaustion on small instance types if tenant bursts are pathological
S3 credentials rotation complexity in Private deployments requiring careful rollout
Replayer could create bursty load on downstream during mass recoveries; must ensure global token-bucket throttling
Schema drift between legacy jaeger payloads and canonical envelope — we add a normalizer with sampling for unknown tags
testing_plan: Unit tests for WAL rotation and checkpointing
Integration test: Tempo mocked to return 503 for 15 minutes then recover; assert expected replay behavior
Load test: synthetic span generator to create 10k tps per host and validate shed/429 semantics
Chaos run: kill sidecar process mid-replay to verify resume/duplication semantics
Security test: validate KMS-encrypted spill objects cannot be read without key rotation mismatch
